nodes.title: SG-5.2 · Scheduler auto-opens due rounds and auto-closes expired rounds
nodes.body:
Context: backend/internal/round/scheduler.go defines Scheduler.Tick, which reads the injected Clock and calls Controller.Open for SCHEDULED rounds whose StartsAt has passed and Controller.Close for OPEN rounds whose EndsAt has passed. Errors are joined with errors.Join so one failure does not stop the pass. Current state: the four TestTick_* tests in scheduler_test.go pass on the repository tip (go test -count=1 ./internal/round/ is ok). Desired behavior: the scheduler keeps this contract. Expected result: due rounds open, expired rounds close, future and other-status rounds are ignored, and closing continues after an open failure. Why: the lifecycle must advance without admin action.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a SCHEDULED round whose StartsAt is not after the clock time, when Tick runs, then Controller.Open is called once for that round.
- Given an OPEN round whose EndsAt is not after the clock time, when Tick runs, then Controller.Close is called once for that round.
- Given future SCHEDULED or OPEN rounds and rounds in other statuses, when Tick runs, then no Controller call is made until the clock reaches the boundary.
- Given Controller.Open returns an error, when Tick runs, then Close for another expired OPEN round still runs and Tick returns an error wrapping the open error.


## Scope
- In scope: backend/internal/round/scheduler.go Tick behavior
- In scope: scheduler unit tests using a fake clock and fake controller
- Out of scope: Lifecycle Open/Close implementation
- Out of scope: admin routes
- Out of scope: frontend
- Preserve: Scheduler, Clock, Controller and Lister exported types
- Preserve: errors.Join aggregation in Tick
- Preserve: Run loop and defaultInterval


## Technical constraints
- Go; no database; the clock must be injected through Scheduler.Clock
- Tests must not use real time or real controllers


## Definition of done
- All four TestTick_* tests pass with go test -count=1
- No other behavior of the round package changes


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Tick opens due SCHEDULED rounds and closes expired OPEN rounds using the injected clock
nodes.body:
Context: Scheduler.Tick in backend/internal/round/scheduler.go uses a switch on rd.Status with !now.Before(rd.StartsAt) for SCHEDULED and !now.Before(rd.EndsAt) for OPEN. Desired behavior: due rounds open and expired rounds close exactly at the boundary. Expected result: one Open or Close call per due round. Why: automatic round lifecycle.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a SCHEDULED round with StartsAt earlier than the clock, when Tick runs, then Open is called with the world and round IDs.
- Given an OPEN round with EndsAt earlier than the clock, when Tick runs, then Close is called with the world and round IDs.
- Given the clock equals StartsAt or EndsAt exactly, when Tick runs, then the round is acted on.


## Scope
- In scope: Open and Close dispatch in Tick
- Out of scope: Controller implementation
- Preserve: Controller interface signatures


## Technical constraints
- Use Scheduler.clock() so a nil Clock falls back to systemClock


## Definition of done
- Open and Close dispatch matches the acceptance criteria


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Tick ignores future rounds and rounds in other statuses and keeps closing after an open failure
nodes.body:
Context: Tick skips rounds not matching either case and collects errors in errs, returning errors.Join(errs...). Desired behavior: failure to open one round never prevents closing another. Expected result: Tick returns an error wrapping the open error while Close still runs. Why: a stuck round must not block expiry of others.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given future SCHEDULED, future OPEN and COMPLETED rounds, when Tick runs before the boundary, then no Controller call is made.
- Given Open returns an error for one round, when Tick runs, then Close is still called for an expired OPEN round.
- Given Open returns an error, when Tick returns, then errors.Is(err, openErr) is true.


## Scope
- In scope: Skip logic and error aggregation in Tick
- Out of scope: Run loop logging
- Preserve: errors.Join return value
- Preserve: error wrapping with %w


## Technical constraints
- Do not return early from the per-round loop on a Controller error


## Definition of done
- Skip and continue-on-error behavior matches the acceptance criteria


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: Act: Confirm Tick open and close dispatch against the injected clock
nodes.body:
Scheduler.Tick already dispatches Open and Close using clock.Now(). This unit keeps that code correct: the boundary comparison uses !now.Before so a time equal to StartsAt or EndsAt counts as due. No behavior change is expected unless the Verify unit finds a mismatch.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a SCHEDULED round with StartsAt not after the clock, when Tick runs, then Controller.Open is called.
- Given an OPEN round with EndsAt not after the clock, when Tick runs, then Controller.Close is called.


## Scope
- In scope: backend/internal/round/scheduler.go Tick switch cases
- Out of scope: tests
- Preserve: Public API of the round package


## Technical constraints
- Clock must come from s.clock()
- Code path: `backend/internal/round/scheduler.go`


## Definition of done
- Tick switch cases use !now.Before(StartsAt) and !now.Before(EndsAt)
- go build ./internal/round/ succeeds


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: Act: Confirm Tick skips non-due rounds and continues after Controller errors
nodes.body:
The Tick loop appends wrapped errors to errs and continues, returning errors.Join(errs...). Rounds with other statuses or future boundaries match no case. This unit keeps that code correct and changes nothing unless the Verify unit finds a mismatch.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given Open fails for one round, when Tick runs, then the loop still processes the remaining rounds.
- Given a round matching no case, when Tick runs, then no Controller call is made.


## Scope
- In scope: backend/internal/round/scheduler.go error aggregation in Tick
- Out of scope: tests
- Preserve: fmt.Errorf %w wrapping
- Preserve: errors.Join result


## Technical constraints
- No early return inside the round loop on Controller errors
- Code path: `backend/internal/round/scheduler.go`


## Definition of done
- Open and Close errors are appended to errs and the loop continues
- go build ./internal/round/ succeeds


## Clarifying questions
- None
